run: pkill -x lms 2>/dev/null; pkill -x llmster 2>/dev/null; sleep 2; rm -rf "$HOME/.lmstudio"; sleep 1; [ -d "$HOME/.lmstudio" ] && exit 1; exit 0

$root = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.lmstudio'; Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Where-Object { ($_.ExecutablePath -and $_.ExecutablePath.StartsWith($root)) -or ($_.CommandLine -and $_.CommandLine.Contains($root)) } | ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; Start-Sleep -Seconds 3; Remove-Item -LiteralPath $root -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Start-Sleep -Seconds 1; if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $root) { exit 1 }

list_models.description: List models available on this system (native REST v1).

loaded_models.description: List models currently loaded in memory (native REST v1, filtered by nonempty loaded_instances).

pull_model.description: Download a model via the lms CLI (params: {"model": "<owner/name | huggingface.co or lmstudio.ai URL>"}). Tries the value as given, then the LM Studio Hub artifact id, then the Hugging Face repo URL. Resumes automatically on a transient download timeout.

load_model.description: Load a downloaded model into memory (params: {"model": "<name>"}).

list_downloaded.description: List models downloaded to disk via the lms CLI.

delete_model.description: Delete a downloaded model from disk and restart the server (params: {"model": "<modelKey | owner/repo | on-disk path>"}). LM Studio serves its model list from an index built at startup and offers no rescan, so a running server keeps advertising the deleted model until it restarts.
